Looking at this PR carefully, I need to verify the changes compile and behave correctly.

**Critical issue:** In `UsernameForm.java` line 47, `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is called with no arguments, but the only method defined is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in the parent `UsernamePasswordForm`. This is a compile error.

**Behavior change:** In `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate()`, the `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` call was moved from inside the `else` block (initial login, user is null) to outside the block, gated on `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` which requires `user != null`. This means the webauthn form data is no longer filled on the initial login page, breaking conditional UI passkey login for users who haven't yet authenticated. The existing test `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest` asserts the webauthn form must be present on the initial login page, which will fail with the new code unless something else fills the form.

**Test code smell:** The try/catch with `fail()` pattern in `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` is awkward for asserting element absence — `assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` is clearer and already used elsewhere in the same package.

findings.title: Compile error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called with no args
findings.body: The method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is invoked with no arguments, but the only definition in the parent class UsernamePasswordForm is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` which requires a UserModel parameter. There is no no-arg overload anywhere in the class hierarchy. This will prevent the project from compiling. Likely intended to be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, or a separate no-arg overload was forgotten.

findings.title: WebAuthn form no longer filled on initial login (conditional UI regression)
findings.body: Before this change the call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` lived inside the `else` branch where `context.getUser() == null`, i.e. it ran on the initial login page so conditional UI passkeys worked for users without a session. The new code hoists it out and gates it on `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which requires `user != null`. As a result the WebAuthn challenge, RP ID, allowed authenticators, and ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI attribute are never set on the initial login form, so navigator.credentials.get() cannot auto-discover passkeys. The existing test `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` still asserts `driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']"))` is present immediately after `oauth.openLoginForm()` (before any submission), which this change makes impossible. The fill must also happen in the `user == null` branch (or in both branches).

findings.title: Awkward try-fail pattern to assert element absence
findings.body: In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, the test uses `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception nsee) {}` to assert that the webauthn button is not rendered. `WebDriver.findElement` throws `NoSuchElementException` when the element is missing and never returns null, so `assertThat(element, nullValue())` would always fail with an AssertionError if the element exists, making the subsequent `fail()` unreachable. The cleaner pattern already used elsewhere in this package (`PasskeysUsernameFormTest` line 202) is `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> driver.findElement(...))`. The same anti-pattern is repeated at line 312.
